## The Problem {.slide-section background-color="#FAFAF8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
The Analogy
:::

### Your AI is doing a Wally {.section-title}

Wally (from *See No Evil, Hear No Evil*) performs sight using memorised cues. He narrates the world he was trained to expect — not the one in front of him[cite: 3].

::: {.vs-grid}

::: {.vs-col .vs-bad}
**What It Claims**

✕ The machine can now "see"  
✕ Native visual understanding  
✕ Reasoning from raw pixels  
✕ Objective perception of reality
:::

::: {.vs-col .vs-good}
**What It Does**

✓ Converts pixels to words first  
✓ Reasons about linguistic tokens  
✓ Describes what it *expects* to see  
✓ Statistical grammar as "sight"
:::

:::

## The Language Bottleneck {.slide-section background-color="#FAFAF8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
The Architecture
:::

### Models *Narrate* Vision. They don't experience it. {.section-title}

Traditional AI systems translate lived experience into abstraction before acting on it[cite: 3].

::: {.mesh-grid}

::: {.mesh-node}
◈
**PIXELS**  
Visual input enters  
the system
:::

::: {.mesh-node .node-teal}
⟳
**TOKENS**  
Converted to language  
before reasoning
:::

::: {.mesh-node .node-amber}
◉
**EXPECTED WORLD**  
Hallucinating with  
trained confidence
:::

:::

> *"Relying on linguistic priors — hallucinating with pre-trained confidence, not seeing."*

## The Illusion {.slide-section background-color="#FAFAF8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
The Metric
:::

### Beauty is Not Meaning {.section-title}

::: {.two-col}

::: {.left-col}
Midjourney knows what beauty looks like, but not what it *means*. The perception is absent; only the vocabulary remains intact[cite: 3].

::: {.card-amber}
**Beautiful ≠ True**  
These models have mastered the statistical grammar of aesthetics. They do not know that glass shatters, nor that wine is liquid.
:::

:::

::: {.stat-col}

::: {.stat-card}
::: {.stat-big}
30%
:::
Accuracy on scientific visual reasoning tasks
:::

::: {.stat-card}
::: {.stat-big}
1989
:::
The year Wally taught us about narrating the void
:::

:::

:::

## Where it Breaks {.slide-section background-color="#FAFAF8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
The Impact
:::

### Spatial Truth Collapses {.section-title}

::: {.tier-grid}

::: {.tier-card}
[01 · Space]{.tier-badge}
**AI cannot parse space**
Spatial relationships — where things are relative to each other — vanish in translation.
[Spatial logic evaporates]{.tier-outcome}
:::

::: {.tier-card .tier-featured}
[02 · Cost]{.tier-badge .badge-teal}
**The marginalized pay**
Visual description omits the structural info that blind and low-vision users depend on.
[The wrong people bear the cost]{.tier-outcome .outcome-teal}
:::

::: {.tier-card .tier-amber}
[03 · Meaning]{.tier-badge .badge-amber}
**Proximity vanishes**
The visual grammar of arrangement disappears. Wally cannot give directions.
[Logic vs Observation]{.tier-outcome .outcome-amber}
:::

:::

## The Differentiator {.slide-section background-color="#FAFAF8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
The Design Mirror
:::

### This is a *Design* Problem {.section-title}

This is not an AI failure; it is an organisational failure to value proximity over assumption[cite: 3].

::: {.adv-grid}

::: {.card-amber}
**Assumption Over Proximity**  
Organisations route insight through assumption, not proximity — and call it research.
:::

::: {.card-teal}
**Experience Gap**  
Expertise without lived experience builds things that are beautiful and wrong.
:::

::: {.card-plain}
**Expectation Trap**  
You design for the world you expect. Your users inhabit a different one.
:::

::: {.card-plain}
**Strategic Steering**  
Reason natively in context. Don't translate experience into abstraction before acting.
:::

:::

## Ready to Start *Perceiving?* {.slide-cta background-color="#FAFAF8"}

::: {.hero-rule}
:::

Stop narrating. Start perceiving. Proximity is a design method, not a values statement[cite: 3].
